block.prompt:
You are going to hear the opening of a radio programme called “The Long View”. Read the four questions below FIRST. Then listen — your teacher will read the recording aloud twice — and note down what you hear.

[Your teacher reads:]
“Good evening, and welcome to The Long View. Tonight: the places we are loving to death. Fifty years ago, foreign travel was a luxury. Today, cheap flights and social media have put almost every corner of the planet within reach — and some of the world's most beautiful places are struggling under the weight of their own fame. Take Hallstatt, the tiny lakeside village in Upper Austria. Fewer than eight hundred people live there. Yet on a busy summer's day, the mayor says, as many as ten thousand visitors arrive — many staying less than an hour, just long enough to take a photograph and move on. Venice now charges day-trippers a fee to enter on its busiest weekends. In Barcelona, residents have marched through the streets with a blunt message for tourists: go home. Tonight we ask a simple question with no simple answer — who does a place belong to?”

1. Which two developments have put travel within reach of far more people today?
2. How many people live in Hallstatt, and how many visitors can arrive on a busy summer's day?
3. What has the city of Venice introduced?
4. What have residents in Barcelona done, and what is their message?
block.answer_key: 1. Cheap flights and social media. 2. Fewer than 800 people live there; up to 10,000 visitors can arrive on a busy summer's day. 3. An entry fee for day-trippers on its busiest weekends. 4. They have marched / protested through the streets; their message is “(tourists) go home”.
watch_outs: Zahlen sind die klassische Hörfalle: ‚fewer than eight hundred' (Einwohner) darf nicht mit ‚ten thousand' (Besucher) verwechselt werden — langsam und deutlich vorlesen, die Zahlen leicht betonen.
‚Loving to death' und ‚under the weight of their own fame' sind Redewendungen (etwas durch Übermaß zerstören) — nicht wörtlich verstehen; ggf. nach dem ersten Durchgang kurz klären.
Ehrlichkeitshinweis für die Lehrkraft: Die genannten Zahlen sind Aussagen des (fiktiven) Radioberichts — gerundete, plausible Richtwerte für die Hörübung, keine geprüfte Statistik.
